judgements.justification: A's Reviewer_1kmf called novelty limited on references that do not prune SR networks (one a 2009 kernel-filter paper), and B's Reviewer_chSU praised the 'first attempt' claim that DHP and the ICASSP 2020 paper contradict.
B's spotlight rests on unanimous confidence-5 8s, which support that tier on their own even though the meta-review adds no reason.
All reviewers judged the paper as an SR pruning method; no one objected to its framing from a neighbouring field's premises.
B's Reviewer_DsQ3 spent 15 hours and held 8, while A's most positive reviewer, k8sL, wrote a three-sentence review in 1 hour and then sided with the critics, so no one in A argued for the paper.
Neither committee rejected the paper because the promised revisions were too large to accept without another review.
Both area chairs relied only on the visible reviews; no off-record assessment appears.
A's objections were novelty and small margins over 2020 baselines, not a standard tied to a contribution type that B did not apply.
A's low scores rested on novelty and missing baselines, which are central to the contribution, not peripheral points.
